 2.1.6 Non-Debt Capital Receipts (NDCR) 
 The main components of Non-Debt Capital Receipts (NDCR) are miscellaneous capital 
receipts and rece ipts from the recovery of loans and advances.  NDCR of the government were 
budgeted at ₹84,000 crore in FY 2023 -24. Out of this, ₹61,000 crore were from miscellaneous 
capital receipts and ₹23,000 crore from the recovery of loans and advances. In RE 2023 -24, 
NDCR was revised to ₹56,000 crore. Against this, the actual (Provisional) receipts under NDCR 
stood at ₹60,460 crore, of which ₹33,122 crore was realized from miscellaneous capital receipts 
and ₹27,338 crore were from the recovery of loans and advances.  
2.2 Expenditure 
In BE 2023-24, the total expenditure of Union Government was estimated at ₹45.03 lakh 
crore which was revised to ₹44.90 lakh crore in RE 2023 -24. The Actual (provisional) 
expenditure in FY 2023 -24 was ₹44.43 lakh crore, recording a growth of 5.9 percent over FY 
2022-23.  
2.2.1 Revenue Expenditure 
Revenue expenditure in BE 2023-24 was estimated at ₹35.02 lakh crore. It was revised to 
₹35.40 lakh crore  in RE 2023 -24. Against this, total revenue expenditure (Provisional) in FY 
2023-24 was ₹34.94 lakh crore. Revenue expenditure accounted for 78.6 per cent of Total 
Expenditure in FY 2023 -24 as compared to 82.4 per cent in FY2022 -23. Out of ₹34.94 lakh 
crore of Revenue Expenditure in FY 2023 -24, ₹3.04 lakh crore was on account of Grant -in-Aid 
for creation of capital assets. 
In FY 2023 -24, around ₹26.16 lakh crore was spent on Interest payments, Defence 
Services, Pension, Major Subsidies and Grants-in-Aids to States/UTs Expenditure (Table 2). The 
revenue expenditure of the above -mentioned heads increased by ₹7404 crore in FY 2023 -24      
as compared to FY 2022-23.

3
SALIENT FEATURES
1. The total expenditure on Pay and Allowances (excluding Productivity Linked
Bonus/ Ad-hoc Bonus, Honorarium, Encashment of Earned Leave and Travelling
Allowance) for Regular Central Government Civilian employees including employees
of the Union Territories and Missions abroad is₹ 275083.75 crore in 2022-23 as
compared to ₹ 256112.31 crore in 2021-22. Thus, there is an increase in
expenditure by 18971.44 crore over previous year which in relative terms works
out to around 7.41%.
2. The total expenditure on pay and allowances as a percentage of Revenue
Expenditure of the Central Government during the financial year 2022-23 is 7.05%
as compared to 7.44% during the financial year 2021-22.
3. Almost 80.48% of the total expenditure of Central Government was incurred
by four major Ministries/ Departments (Railways, Defence (Civil), Home Affairs and
Posts) during 2022-23.
4. Of the total expenditure on Pay and Allowances in 2022-23, the Ministry of
Railways continues to have the largest share i.e. 36.39%, marginally increasing from
36.17% in 2021-22. Share of Ministry of Home Affairs is 27.88%, marginally
decreasing from 28.80 in 2021-22 and Department of Posts has decreased from
5.46% to 4.95%. Share of Ministry of Defence (Civil) has decreased from 12.15% to
11.26%.
5. The expenditure of UT Administrations is 5565.15 crore in 2022-23 as
compared to 4896.09 crore in 2021-22. Thus, there is an increase in expenditure by
669.06 crore over previous year which in relative terms works out to around
13.67%.
6. The expenditure of Indian Missions/ Embassies abroad is ₹1929.43 crore in
2022-23 as compared to ₹1623.56 crore in 2021-22. Thus, there is an increase in
expenditure by ₹305.87 crore over previous year which in relative terms works out to
around 18.84%.
According to the ten-year expenditure table, by how much did annual pay and allowances expenditure grow between 2019-20 and 2022-23, in rupees crore?
